note: A study map of the main rules, not legal advice. Thresholds and dates change; confirm with counsel and the regulator's current text before acting.

jurisdictions.name: European Union (cross-border)
jurisdictions.regulator: National regulators (CSSF, AMF, BaFin, CBI…) coordinated by ESMA
jurisdictions.summary: The EU regulates the manager, not the fund. AIFMD sets authorisation, depositary, reporting and marketing rules for anyone managing alternative funds in or into the EU. AIFMD II applied from 16 April 2026. Product regimes (ELTIF, EuVECA) and disclosure rules (SFDR, fund names) sit on top.
laws: AIFMD, Directive 2011/61/EU
AIFMD II, Directive (EU) 2024/927, applied from 16 April 2026; some reporting changes from 16 April 2027
Cross-border distribution: Directive (EU) 2019/1160 and Regulation (EU) 2019/1156
ELTIF Regulation as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/606 (ELTIF 2.0), applying from 10 January 2024; RTS in force 26 October 2024
EuVECA Regulation (EU) 345/2013
SFDR, Regulation (EU) 2019/2088; SFDR 2.0 proposal of 20 November 2025
ESMA Guidelines on funds' names using ESG or sustainability terms
AML Directives and the EU AML package
vehicles: Any national AIF form (SCSp, SLP, KG, ILP…)
ELTIF: EU-wide product authorisation for long-term private market funds, open to retail
EuVECA: label for venture funds marketed to professionals and to others committing at least €100,000
jurisdictions.licensing: A full AIFM licence is required above €100 million AUM with leverage, or €500 million unleveraged with no redemption rights for five years. Below that, sub-threshold managers register nationally and may opt in. Many emerging managers use a third-party AIFM.
jurisdictions.marketing: An authorised EU AIFM can passport an EU AIF to professional investors across the EU by notification. Pre-marketing is allowed but must be notified to the home regulator within two weeks, and any subscription within 18 months of pre-marketing counts as the result of marketing. Non-EU funds and managers use national private placement regimes country by country.
jurisdictions.investors: Professional investors under MiFID by default. Retail access only through ELTIF, or national regimes that allow semi-professionals (for example France's €100,000 / €30,000 rules).
thresholds: Above €100m leveraged / €500m unleveraged and closed for 5 years
At least two under AIFMD II
ongoing: Annex IV reporting to the home regulator
Annual report within six months of year end
Depositary oversight of cash, custody and compliance
Valuation at least annually, independent or functionally separate
SFDR pre-contractual and periodic disclosures for Article 8 and 9 funds
Delegation oversight; AIFMD II tightens reporting on delegation
recent: AIFMD II applies: loan-origination regime, mandatory liquidity tools for open-ended AIFs, more fee and delegation disclosure.
Commission publishes SFDR 2.0 proposal replacing Articles 8/9 with Transition, ESG Basics and Sustainable categories. Application not expected before 2029.
ESMA fund names guidelines apply to new funds from May 2025 and existing funds from November 2025.
ELTIF 2.0 RTS enter into force, setting redemption, holding period and liquidity rules.
pitfalls: Starting pre-marketing and then relying on reverse solicitation
Using 'ESG', 'green' or 'sustainable' in a fund name without meeting ESMA thresholds
Treating the passport as covering non-professional investors

jurisdictions.name: Luxembourg
jurisdictions.regulator: CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier)
jurisdictions.summary: Europe's main fund domicile. Most private funds use an SCSp or SCS partnership, either unregulated (managed by an authorised AIFM) or as a RAIF. SIFs and SICARs remain for funds that want direct CSSF supervision.
laws: AIFM Law of 12 July 2013, amended by the Law of 3 March 2026 transposing AIFMD II
RAIF Law of 23 July 2016
SIF Law of 13 February 2007
SICAR Law of 15 June 2004
Companies Law of 10 August 1915 (SCSp, SCS, SCA, SA)
AML Law of 12 November 2004
vehicles: SCSp: special limited partnership, no legal personality, tax transparent
SCS: limited partnership with legal personality
RAIF: not approved by CSSF, must have an authorised AIFM; can be SIF-like or SICAR-like
SIF and SICAR: CSSF-approved products
jurisdictions.licensing: The AIFM may be a Luxembourg ManCo authorised by the CSSF or an EU AIFM using its management passport. RAIFs must appoint an authorised AIFM.
jurisdictions.marketing: EU passport for professional investors; well-informed investors only for RAIF/SIF.
jurisdictions.investors: Well-informed investors: institutional or professional investors, or others who confirm in writing and invest at least €100,000 or have a bank, investment firm or ManCo assessment.
thresholds: Notarial deed, registration with RCS; no CSSF approval
Filed via CSSF module by 16 April 2026
ongoing: AML/CFT compliance and RC (responsable du contrôle) appointment
recent: Law transposing AIFMD II; in force 16 April 2026 with some reporting deferred to 16 April 2027.
Mar–Apr 2026
CSSF requires open-ended AIFMs to file liquidity tool selections.
pitfalls: Assuming a RAIF can be marketed to retail
refs: CSSF website: AIFM and RAIF pages

jurisdictions.name: France
jurisdictions.summary: France has professional private equity vehicles that need only a declaration to the AMF, and retail vehicles that need approval. Institutional funds mostly use the FPCI or the SLP (French limited partnership, created in 2015).
laws: Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier)
AMF General Regulation, Book IV, Title II (AIFs)
AMF Instruction DOC-2012-06 (declared funds)
vehicles: FPCI: professional private equity fund, declared not authorised; at least 50% in unlisted companies
SLP: société de libre partenariat, partnership-style LPA
FPS and OFS: professional specialised and financing funds
FCPR, FCPI, FIP: retail vehicles approved by the AMF
jurisdictions.licensing: French AIFM (société de gestion de portefeuille) authorised by the AMF, or an EU AIFM passporting in.
jurisdictions.marketing: Professional funds may be set up without AMF authorisation except for marketing. Non-French AIFMs marketing in France pay a fixed annual fee per fund.
jurisdictions.investors: FPCI: professional investors; investors subscribing €100,000 or more; or €30,000 or more meeting experience conditions. SLP: professional investors and, under conditions, others from €100,000.
thresholds: €2,000 per fund per year (2025 practice guide)
ongoing: Declaration to AMF within one month of creation (FPCI)
Annual report and audited accounts by statutory auditor
recent: Updated AMF General Regulation articles on professional funds in force.
pitfalls: Marketing an FPCI to non-eligible individuals
Assuming French carried interest tax treatment without meeting holding and investment conditions

jurisdictions.name: Monaco
jurisdictions.regulator: CCAF (Commission de Contrôle des Activités Financières); AML supervision by AMSF
jurisdictions.summary: Monaco is not in the EU and has no AIFMD passport. Fund management and investment services from Monaco need CCAF authorisation, usually through a SAM. Marketing to Monaco private residents is reserved to CCAF-authorised firms. Monaco left the FATF grey list in October 2026.
laws: Law 1.338 of 7 September 2007 on financial activities
Law 1.339 of 7 September 2007 on mutual funds and investment funds
Sovereign Ordinances 1.284 and 1.285
Law 1.515 (canvassing restrictions) and Law 1.529 of 29 July 2022 (marketing clarification)
Law 1.362 of 3 August 2009 on AML/CFT, as amended
vehicles: Monaco FCP (fonds commun de placement) and investment funds under Law 1.339, including funds holding non-financial assets
Foreign funds (UCITS, AIFs) distributed through CCAF-authorised firms
jurisdictions.licensing: Any person providing investment services or managing funds in or from Monaco on a professional basis needs prior CCAF authorisation. EU licences do not passport into Monaco.
jurisdictions.marketing: Firms not authorised by the CCAF may not market financial services or products to Monaco private residents, whether solicited or not, with limited exceptions. Foreign products can be marketed by Monaco-authorised firms under their own liability. Check fund-level conditions with the CCAF before distributing.
jurisdictions.investors: Depends on the vehicle and distributor's licence; professional and private client rules apply through the CCAF-licensed firm.
ongoing: AML/CFT programme under Law 1.362; enhanced due diligence expectations from EU counterparties
recent: FATF removes Monaco from its grey list after significant progress on AML/CFT.
Monaco added to the EU list of high-risk third countries; EU firms apply enhanced due diligence. Check whether the EU list has been updated after FATF removal.
pitfalls: Assuming an EU AIFM can market in Monaco on its passport
A single mandate or pitch to a Monaco resident without CCAF authorisation can be an unlicensed activity

jurisdictions.name: India (SEBI)
jurisdictions.regulator: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)
jurisdictions.summary: Domestic pooled funds are AIFs under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012. Most are trusts with a sponsor, a trustee and a manager. Each scheme is filed with SEBI through a merchant banker. 2025–26 brought Accredited Investors only Funds, a lower Large Value Fund threshold and a new winding-up framework.
laws: SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations 2012, as amended
SEBI Master Circular for AIFs (updated June 2026)
SEBI (AIF) (Third Amendment) Regulations 2025 (notified 18 Nov 2025)
SEBI (AIF) Amendment Regulations of 18 April 2026 and circular of 16 June 2026 (winding up)
Income-tax Act provisions on pass-through (section 115UB)
FEMA rules on foreign-owned AIFs
vehicles: Category I: VC (including angel funds), SME, social impact, infrastructure
Category II: PE, private credit, others; no leverage beyond operational needs
Category III: hedge-style, leverage allowed
Accredited Investors only Fund (AIOF) and Large Value Fund (LVF)
jurisdictions.licensing: The AIF itself registers with SEBI. Sponsor and manager must be fit and proper. Compliance officers of AIF managers need NISM certification.
jurisdictions.marketing: Private placement only, through the PPM filed with SEBI. No public offer.
jurisdictions.investors: Minimum ₹1 crore per investor (₹25 lakh for employees and directors). Accredited investors exempt. Angel funds: accredited investors only. Up to 1,000 non-accredited investors per scheme.
thresholds: Lower of 2.5% of corpus or ₹5 crore
Higher of 0.5% of each investment or ₹50,000
recent: SEBI circular sets conditions for retaining liquidation proceeds beyond fund life and an Inoperative Fund status.
AIF Regulations amended for flexibility in winding up and surrender of registration.
Third Amendment creates Accredited Investors only Funds; LVF threshold cut to ₹25 crore.
Sep 2025
Angel fund framework revised; continuing interest moved to deal level.
pitfalls: Meeting continuing interest through fee waivers (not allowed)
Holding first close before minimum corpus
Missing the liquidation period deadline at end of tenure
refs: SEBI AIF Regulations 2012 and Master Circular

jurisdictions.name: India (GIFT IFSC)
jurisdictions.summary: GIFT City in Gujarat is India's international financial centre, with its own regulator and dollar-denominated funds. Fund management entities (FMEs) register with IFSCA and launch venture capital, restricted (non-retail) or retail schemes.
laws: IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations 2025, notified 19 February 2025 (replacing the 2022 regulations)
IFSCA transition guidelines of 8 April 2025
Amendments approved 22 December 2025
vehicles: Venture Capital Scheme (treated as a Category I VC fund)
Restricted scheme (non-retail)
Retail scheme
Special situation fund
jurisdictions.licensing: FME registration with IFSCA, with substance and key personnel in GIFT City.
jurisdictions.marketing: Private placement for non-retail schemes; PPM taken on record by IFSCA.
jurisdictions.investors: Venture capital scheme: at most 50 investors, each at least USD 250,000; accredited investors permitted. Close-ended only.
thresholds: 12 months from PPM on record; one-time 6-month extension
Can begin investing at USD 1 million
recent: IFSCA approves amendments including one-time extension windows for schemes that missed corpus deadlines.
Fund Management Regulations 2025 notified.
pitfalls: Letting the PPM lapse before reaching minimum corpus
Treating GIFT funds as SEBI AIFs for investor rules
refs: IFSCA press release on FM Regulations 2025

jurisdictions.name: United States
jurisdictions.regulator: SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission); CFTC for commodity interests
jurisdictions.summary: US private funds avoid registration as investment companies through sections 3(c)(1) or 3(c)(7) and raise money under Regulation D. Advisers register with the SEC or rely on exemptions. The 2023 Private Fund Adviser Rules were vacated in June 2024; Form PF amendments are delayed.
laws: Investment Company Act of 1940, sections 3(c)(1) and 3(c)(7)
Investment Advisers Act of 1940
Securities Act of 1933, Regulation D (Rules 506(b) and 506(c))
SEC Marketing Rule 206(4)-1
Form PF and Form ADV
vehicles: Delaware limited partnership
Delaware LLC
Cayman exempted LP for offshore feeders
jurisdictions.licensing: SEC registration for advisers above thresholds. Exemptions for venture capital fund advisers and private fund advisers with less than $150 million in US private fund AUM (exempt reporting advisers still file parts of Form ADV).
jurisdictions.marketing: Rule 506(b): no general solicitation, accredited investors (plus limited non-accredited). Rule 506(c): general solicitation allowed, all investors verified accredited. Registered advisers follow the Marketing Rule on performance presentation.
jurisdictions.investors: 3(c)(1): generally up to 100 beneficial owners. 3(c)(7): qualified purchasers only.
thresholds: Within 90 days of fiscal year end (31 March for calendar year)
ongoing: Form PF (annual for PE advisers; quarterly event reports)
Annual audit and delivery of audited financials (custody rule)
Code of ethics and personal trading reports
recent: SEC and CFTC extend Form PF compliance date to 1 July 2027 and propose raising the filing threshold to $1 billion.
Jun 2024
Fifth Circuit vacates Private Fund Adviser Rules; ILPA templates fill the reporting gap.
pitfalls: Showing gross performance without net under the Marketing Rule
refs: SEC Release IA-6992 (Form PF compliance date)
Kirkland and Paul Weiss 2026 compliance calendars

jurisdictions.name: United Kingdom
jurisdictions.summary: The UK kept AIFMD after Brexit and is now redesigning it. The 2026 proposals replace today's thresholds with three NAV-based tiers and abolish the small registered regime for most managers. Implementation is envisaged for 2028.
laws: Alternative Investment Fund Managers Regulations 2013 (current)
Draft Alternative Investment Fund Managers Regulations 2026 (HM Treasury)
FCA CP26/28: The UK AIFM Regime (14 July 2026)
Limited Partnerships Act 1907; private fund limited partnership (PFLP) since 2017
vehicles: English LP or Scottish LP, usually as a PFLP
LTAF for long-term assets
jurisdictions.licensing: Today: full-scope above €100m/€500m; small authorised or small registered below. Proposed: small (under £750m NAV), medium (£750m–£5bn), large (over £5bn); small registered regime removed except for RVECA, SEF and certain internally managed funds.
jurisdictions.marketing: National private placement regime for non-UK funds; financial promotion rules for others.
jurisdictions.investors: Professional investors; restricted promotion to retail.
ongoing: FCA regulatory returns (to be replaced by FRAME reporting under proposals)
Valuation rules proposed for all AIFM sizes
recent: FCA CP26/28 and HM Treasury draft regulations published; consultation closed October 2026.
pitfalls: Assuming EU passport rights after Brexit
Small registered managers planning without the authorisation step

topics.name: Manager licensing
topics.why: Who may manage the fund and under what licence.

by.eu: AIFM authorisation above thresholds; otherwise national registration or third-party AIFM.
by.lu: CSSF-authorised AIFM or passported EU AIFM; RAIF must use authorised AIFM.
by.fr: AMF-authorised portfolio management company or passported AIFM.
by.mc: Prior CCAF authorisation, usually via a SAM; no passport.
by.in: AIF registers with SEBI; sponsor and manager fit and proper; NISM-certified compliance officer.
by.ifsc: FME registration with IFSCA and substance in GIFT City.
by.us: SEC registration or VC / private fund adviser exemption.

topics.name: Marketing and pre-marketing
topics.why: How and to whom the fund can be offered.

by.eu: Passport to professionals; pre-marketing notice within 2 weeks; 18-month rule.
by.lu: EU passport; well-informed investors for RAIF/SIF.
by.fr: Professional funds free to set up, but marketing needs notification; annual fee for non-French AIFMs.
by.mc: Only CCAF-authorised firms may market to Monaco private residents, solicited or not.
by.ifsc: Private placement via PPM taken on record.
by.us: Reg D 506(b)/(c); Marketing Rule for registered advisers.
by.uk: NPPR for non-UK funds; financial promotion rules.

by.eu: Professional investors; retail via ELTIF; EuVECA from €100,000.
by.mc: Through the licensed distributor's client classification.
by.in: ₹1 crore minimum; accredited exempt; AIOF and LVF (₹25 crore).

topics.name: AML, KYC and sanctions
topics.why: Know who the money belongs to.

by.eu: EU AML package; enhanced due diligence for high-risk third countries.
by.lu: AML Law 2004; RC appointment; RBE register.
by.fr: Monetary and Financial Code AML rules; TRACFIN reporting.
by.mc: Law 1.362; AMSF supervision; FATF grey list exit Oct 2026.
by.in: PMLA and SEBI KYC norms; KRA records.
by.us: OFAC sanctions; FinCEN adviser AML rule postponed.

topics.name: Regulatory and investor reporting
topics.why: What goes to regulators and LPs, and when.

by.eu: Annex IV; annual report within six months; AIFMD II reporting changes from 2027.
by.lu: CSSF reporting via AIFM; annual accounts.
by.in: Quarterly SEBI reports; annual PPM audit; benchmarking data.
by.us: Form ADV; Form PF; audited financials to LPs.

topics.name: Valuation
topics.why: How NAV is set and checked.

by.eu: AIFMD valuation function independent or external; at least annual.
by.us: Fair value under US GAAP (ASC 820); IPEV in practice.
by.uk: Proposed to apply to all AIFM sizes.

topics.name: Conflicts and governance
topics.why: Protecting LPs where the manager's interests differ.

by.in: Code of conduct; investor approval for related-party transactions.

by.eu: SFDR Articles 6/8/9 today; SFDR 2.0 categories proposed; ESMA naming rules.
by.fr: SFDR plus French Article 29 Energy-Climate Law reporting.
by.mc: No SFDR; marketing claims still need to be fair.
by.in: No SFDR equivalent for AIFs; BRSR for listed companies.
by.ifsc: IFSCA ESG disclosure guidance for certain schemes.
by.us: No federal fund ESG rule in force.

by.eu: National rules; ATAD; withholding and treaty access.
by.lu: SCSp tax transparent; subscription tax on some vehicles.
by.fr: FPCI and SLP transparent; specific carry regime.
by.mc: No personal income tax for most residents; fund tax per structure.
by.in: Cat I/II pass-through except business income (section 115UB).
by.us: Partnership pass-through; blockers for tax-exempt and foreign LPs.

by.eu: Records kept at least five years.
by.lu: As EU; AML records five years.
by.in: Records for five years after winding up.

by.eu: Per fund documents; regulator and depositary informed.
by.lu: Liquidation per Companies Law and LPA.
by.fr: Liquidation per fund rules; AMF informed.
by.in: 1-year liquidation period; dissolution period with 75% consent; in-specie; Inoperative Fund status (2026).
by.us: Per LPA; Form ADV and Form PF updates.

calendar.item: Pre-marketing notification to home regulator after starting pre-marketing
Minimum corpus raised; continuing interest committed
LP quarterly report with capital account statement (ILPA Reporting Template from Q1 2026)
Form PF event report for PE advisers when a reporting event occurs
Form PF annual update for PE and real estate advisers
Audited annual accounts delivered to LPs
LP annual meeting and LPAC meeting
AML risk assessment and KYC refresh by risk rating
SFDR periodic report for Article 8/9 funds
Liquidation period ends; seek dissolution period (75% consent) or distribute in specie
Keep fund and AML records (longer where local law requires)

checklists.name: Launch compliance
items: Fund registered, declared or filed as required
Valuation, conflicts, AML, personal dealing and data protection policies adopted
Marketing permissions confirmed for each LP country

checklists.name: Every closing
items: KYC and beneficial owners verified for each LP

checklists.name: Every year
items: ESG and SFDR periodic disclosures issued

checklists.name: End of fund
items: Extensions approved per LPA and regulation
Remaining assets realised or distributed in specie
Final waterfall and clawback test done
Reserves for claims set and documented
